06 / CODE

How I write Apex.

A small example of the bulk-safe style I use in triggers.

OpportunityTrigger.trigger
// Sample pattern: a bulkified trigger (illustrative, not client code)
trigger OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity (after update) {
    Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();

    for (Opportunity opp : Trigger.new) {
        if (opp.StageName == 'Closed Won' &&
            Trigger.oldMap.get(opp.Id).StageName != 'Closed Won') {
            accountIds.add(opp.AccountId);
        }
    }
    if (accountIds.isEmpty()) return;

    // One query and one DML statement for the whole batch
    List<Account> accounts = [
        SELECT Id, Customer_Since__c FROM Account WHERE Id IN :accountIds
    ];
    for (Account acc : accounts) {
        if (acc.Customer_Since__c == null) acc.Customer_Since__c = Date.today();
    }
    update accounts;
}

One loop collects the records that changed, then a single query and a single update handle the whole batch. That keeps the trigger inside Salesforce governor limits.
